Does it still make sense to have translations on the SearchBox since it's icon based?

See 
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/123822/22703420/64de70b2-ed64-11e6-8cef-27bda2e52897.png)

https://deploy-preview-1954--algolia-instantsearch.netlify.com/instantsearch.js/react/storybook/?knob-translate=%7B%22submit%22%3A%22submit%22%2C%22reset%22%3A%22test%22%2C%22submitTitle%22%3A%22Submit%20your%20search%20query.%22%2C%22resetTitle%22%3A%22Clear%20your%20search%20query.%22%2C%22placeholder%22%3A%22Search%20your%20website.%22%7D&selectedKind=SearchBox&selectedStory=playground&full=0&down=1&left=1&panelRight=1&downPanel=kadirahq%2Fstorybook-addon-knobs

I think we should keep it as some people are already using it in a "button first" way. 

I didn't remember that the playground was using values for those buttons. Maybe we could just remove them by default?

@shakefu, going further we would like to propose you to have:

```jsx
<SearchBox
  resetComponent={() => 'reset'}
  submitComponent={() => 'Submit'}
/>
```

Since we switched to an icon based default searchbox, providing translations for reset and submit is no more relevant, we are not translating anything here, just hacking around.

That's why we think letting you provide your own reset and submit components is maybe the best idea, so you could even configure icons.

Another solution for you would be to switch to [connectSearchBox](https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/react/connectors/connectSearchBox.html) since you are willing to change the complete design of it now.

What do you think?
Closing since we will probably do something different given @shakefu answer

cc @shakefu interested in the proposal? Anyone else interested chime in so we know it's something you would like.

Also maybe @Haroenv since you tried to style the actual searchbox lately
Would that make more sense if the *component were a react element (like: ```jsx } submitComponent={() => search} /> ``` Or is that actually the same?
@vvo @Haroenv Either solution (translation string in prop or JSX element in prop) would work really well!

> Or is that actually the same?

I was not precise enough, this is what I want to provide. @Haroenv wanna have a try at a first code contribution to react-instantsearch? Go for it!
